asked.asked:
**Repository:** JKershaw/LinearViewer (Harbour).

**What this is for.** John: "Side rail and other UI improvements are important purely because the current ones are just mostly the original ones and are due a bit of a sprinkling. But! The front end code is messy." And his gut: "the UI issues trace back to one of my very first rules: no build step… it's the biggest target of the Theseus method… We don't need to tidy it all, but it's a perfect example where we can leave it better than we found it. Likely this will take a fair amount of hand holding."

On main (9 Nov), no browser file can import another, nine browser files restate logic the server already has, and the largest browser file is 5,019 lines.

On the views, John: "Lots of light little views is ideal, but the cost of them has to be balanced… I'd be sad to get rid, but happy to tidy."

**What we want.**

* Browser code that shares rather than restates. There's still no build step and no framework: the rule stays, read as allowing the browser to import, as browsers do natively, and that reading goes into the project's own notes.
* Taken in small slices, one view or one shared piece at a time. Each view is reworked only after finding out why it got so large, and comes out lighter.
* Anything bigger that a slice spots is left out of it and goes into the area's note.
* The side rail and the visual refresh come after, built on the cleaner code.
* No view is retired unless John rules it.

John expects agents to reach for big moves here: "very likely to get agents trying really hard to do big things when we want small." So the size is John's call, and for this work it's small.

**Done when** the reading of the rule is in the project's notes; the first slice has landed, sharing rather than restating, lighter than before and naming what it retired; and John has read the first slice's result before the next starts.

**Every change names what it retires. Questions:** settle engineering questions yourself; only John's calls (product, money, authority, what to retire) go to him as rulings.

Revised after plan-review's request-changes (verdict-35): the blocker (finding-34) is folded in, and the builder notes (finding-36 to 42, finding-24@3). Re-grounded at 4b5001ddf (still origin/main): no commits since 12:08 on any named path. finding-34 verified in source: workspace-kpis.js IIFE calls charts.draw('cost') at top level, chart-helpers draw runs new Chart synchronously, y-axis ticks.callback is window.CostFormat.formatUsd (workspace-kpis.js:138). Fits one session; plan-review due: no (already reviewed; the review said ready to build once the deferral, restated rule and Chart-stub witness were in, and they are).

Which way. (a) Serve through the allow-list: a second frozen map SHARED_MODULES in lib/vendor-assets.js (/shared/cost-format.js -> lib/cost-format.js), statSync at boot, rootDir option beside nodeModulesDir for tests; VENDOR_ASSETS untouched (vendor-assets.test.js pins its three URLs); mount stays just before express.static('public'). Set aside: express.static('lib'); moving the file into public/. (b) Deferred module shim public/cost-format-global.js imports formatUsd and sets window.CostFormat; no view becomes a module, common.js and the vm loaders untouched. Set aside: converting a consumer; keeping public/cost-format.js as a wrapper. (c) lib/components/page.js: a scripts entry may be {module:'/x.js'}, emitted as <script type="module" src>; strings stay classic. (d) Ordering rule, restated: no consumer may read window.CostFormat during script execution, including through a callback a library runs synchronously. flight-companion (DOMContentLoaded), observation (init on DOMContentLoaded) and prompt-section (after a fetch) comply as they are; workspace-kpis.js does not (Chart.js constructor calls ticks.callback). Fix at the cause: run its IIFE body from a DOMContentLoaded listener, early-return guards inside; changes when it draws, not what; not a view rework. Set aside: callbacks tolerating an absent formatter (wrong ticks, silently). (e) Retirement in the same PR (the-second-copy.md s9-10). (f) Shared modules are leaves: no imports, no Node built-ins, no DOM at load.

Places (grep -rIn "cost-format\|CostFormat" outside node_modules, .git and dated docs; rerun after building and read every hit): six renderer lists get the shim: lib/render.js:384, render-flight-companion.js:400, render-observation.js:366, render-swipe.js:149, render-task-page.js:82 (const SCRIPTS), render-workspace-kpis.js:226. Consumers flight-companion.js:428, observation.js:3992, prompt-section.js:1506, workspace-kpis.js:134,138; only workspace-kpis changes behaviour; the other three change comments only (flight-companion.js:419-426, observation.js:3975-3976,3989 'restated here / no module graph', prompt-section.js:1505), counted as comment edits. Golden render-task-page-golden.json via UPDATE_RENDER_TASK_PAGE_GOLDEN=1, diff only the script tags. tests/fixtures/browser-cost-format.js keeps synchronous loadCostFormat(sandbox), statically imports formatUsd, assigns sandbox.window.CostFormat = {formatUsd}; drop COST_FORMAT_SRC. observation-scan-due.test.js:59 switches to loadCostFormat; cost-read.test.js needs nothing (confirm). cost-read-census.test.js FORMAT_ALLOW (line 85), header (14-15), failure text: remove by hand. lib/cost-format.js:12 'browser twin' becomes one line: also served at /shared/cost-format.js, so must stay a leaf. docs/architecture/source-map.md:149 and its vendor-assets line gain the route (run the docs anchor resolver).

Steps. 1 Docs first. CLAUDE.md is 110/110 lines, 11,950/12,000 bytes: rewrite line 43 'Keep it minimal - no frameworks, no build step' in place to a short reading plus a pointer to docs/areas/front-end-browser.md; if over 12,000 bytes, trim elsewhere in the same commit and say what went. Existing statusCode and buildDispatchModelOptionDescriptors entries untouched. 8 PR names the retirements with line counts, the 34-line IIFE against the shim, comment edits apart, total lines may rise (guards are tests), any CLAUDE.md trim; then stop: next slice waits for John.

Witnesses (fail before, pass after): /shared/cost-format.js 200, JavaScript type, exact bytes; unknown /shared/* and /lib/cost-format.js a real 404 through the full server.js app, not the bare router. Router over an empty rootDir throws. Purity over SHARED_MODULES: no import, no node: or bare specifier, no top-level window|document|process|require, checked on code with comments stripped; a synthetic bad module must be named. Ordering, the real one (fails at load today): workspace-kpis.js in loadWorld with CostFormat absent, __WORKSPACE_KPI_DATA__ with nonzero cost.perDay, a Chart stub whose constructor calls each scale ticks.callback: no throw; then install the global, fireDOMContentLoaded (client-world.js:58), assert formatted ticks (without the stub the file returns early and proves nothing). Other three consumers: load with the global absent, no throw, then same strings. Page-has-shim guard: every lib/ list naming a window.CostFormat consumer also lists the shim as {module}, parsing both scripts: [...] and const SCRIPTS = [...]. renderPage emits module vs classic tags. Retirement: both files gone, FORMAT_ALLOW has no public/ entry, census still rejects a hand-made $...toFixed in a new public/ file. One Playwright check on the cheapest spec carrying the shim: formatUsd(0.004) is <$0.01, no console errors, no CSP violation (lib/security-headers.js); it does NOT cover the Chart.js fix (workspace-kpis.spec.js:133-136: priced lineages can't be created, empty note only). Run lin-3833-run-control, flight-companion-client, observation-scan-due, cost-read, cost-read-census, vendor-assets, render-pages, claude-md-line-budget, the docs anchor resolver, the new tests, full unit run.

Likeliest breaks: a page without the shim or a read during script execution (throws on first cost); the module refused (MIME, CSP, URL off the allow-list) so CostFormat never exists, silently; a silent loosening or stale guard (parity assertions dropped, golden, FORMAT_ALLOW, CLAUDE.md budget).

index.line: A page script's second request keeps the poll's discipline: coalesce every reason into one fetch per window, and stop when the poll stops (hidden tab, 401, revoked link). `createTimelineRefresher` (`public/task-page.js`, LIN-4405) is the pattern; a running chip changes the poll's track about once a minute, so "fetch when it changes" alone repeats. Done reads once more first (`finish`): the poll that says done carries the last change, and stopping drops it.

Every page is classic scripts talking through globals: `lib/components/page.js` writes ordered `<script src>` tags, and files read `window.X` and top-level bindings from `public/common.js` (3,309 lines, on 29 pages). A classic script cannot use static `import`; making a view `type="module"` makes it deferred, strict and module-scoped, so its globals vanish for later scripts. "One view at a time" is blocked until what views read from `common.js` is reachable another way. Bigger than a slice: kept out of LIN-4446's first slice, as is view size. (Survey @ 4b5001ddf.)

"Lighter" is easy to fake: about 1,985 of `public/observation.js`'s 5,019 lines are comments (ticket history, retuning stories), and 1,456 of `public/common.js`'s 3,309. Cutting comments passes a line count without sharing anything. Judge "lighter" and the why-so-large check (68 commits on `observation.js`) on logic and commentary counted separately. (Survey @ 4b5001ddf.)
Read the first slice's result (the rule's reading in the notes, and the cost-format slice with what it retired) before the next slice starts.

The comment count in finding-14 does not match mine: I count 1,006 comment lines out of 4,679 non-blank in `public/observation.js` (mostly logic), against finding-14's ~1,985 of 5,019. Before judging "lighter" on logic and commentary counted separately, settle one counting method (blank lines, block vs line comments, JSDoc) and state it in the verdict. (Survey place @ 4b5001ddf.)

On the observation.js comment count: I reproduce finding-14's ~1,985, as 1,985 comment lines of 4,679 non-blank, counting every line that starts with `*`, `//` or `/*`. finding-20's 1,006 counts some other way. Use that method, or name another, when judging "lighter"; the area note's Waiting entry for observation.js states it.

Correction to why prompt-section.js is safe (finding-34 and plan-28 (d) say after a fetch): a fetch started during parsing can resolve before a two-file module graph loads, so that is no guarantee. The real one: every PromptSection.init caller runs at DOMContentLoaded or later: task-page.js:926 on DOMContentLoaded; app.js:2321 init() on DOMContentLoaded, Home prompt mounts after user-triggered fetches via bindHomeFolds; swipe.js:857 when the user opens the prompts section. Use that reason in the corrected comment at prompt-section.js:1505, and drive that consumer witness through init and a resolved decision-panel fetch.

Limits: shared modules are leaves (imports nothing, names no browser or Node global, as the purity guard enforces); served one file at a time through the lib/vendor-assets.js allow-list, never a directory; classic views and the vm test loaders stay until a module-capable client test loader exists; a deferred module shim sets its global after classic scripts run, so no script may read a shared global during script execution, including through a callback a library runs synchronously (Chart.js ticks).
